title: Implement a Global Undo/Redo System for ShowRunner Studio
description: ShowRunner Studio is a feature-rich desktop application for managing live productions. A critical missing feature, frequently requested by users, is a robust Undo/Redo capability. Accidental changes to the Sceneboard or Scriptpad can be destructive and disrupt workflow. This task involves architecting and implementing a global, stack-based Undo/Redo system that can be incrementally adopted by various plugins. The implementation will be done over multiple development sessions, starting with the core framework and then integrating it into a specific plugin.

project_spec.name: ShowRunner Studio
project_spec.description:
ShowRunner Studio is an expert-level, microservice-driven desktop productivity suite that helps streamers, podcasters, game casters, and live-show producers plan, script, cue, and live-switch all facets of an entertainment broadcast from a single multi-window workspace.  Each workspace pane (ScriptPad, SceneBoard, AssetVault, HotKeyDeck, and LiveTimeline) is a separate micro-frontend talking to dedicated back-end services over an event bus, allowing producers to juggle cues, trigger soundboards, reorder scenes, and manage on-the-fly audience interactions without interrupting the live flow.

The platform ships with an extensible plug-in store where third-party developers can drop specialized show gadgets—like adaptive lighting controllers or real-time meme generators—into the runtime without recompiling the core.  A command-pattern action layer, fed through an event-driven state machine, guarantees that every cut, fade, and media swap is undoable and scriptable, while the built-in crash-reporting and auto-update services keep the high-pressure production environment stable and current.
dependencies: ZeroMQ – low-latency event bus for real-time cue routing
SQLite + libsqlcipher – encrypted local project storage
jansson – lightweight JSON serialization for settings and plugins
libcurl – auto-update downloads and crash-report uploads
CMocka – unit-testing framework for plug-in CI
CEF (Chromium Embedded Framework) – optional web-rendered overlays
OpenSSL – secure plug-in signing and update verification
